text: When a ball is dropped into a lake from a height 4.9 m above the water level, it hits the water with a velocity v and then sinks to the bottom with the constant velocity v. It reaches the bottom of the lake 4.0 s after it is dropped. The approximate depth of the lake is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$t_{1}=\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}$

$=\sqrt{\frac{2\times 4.9}{9.8}}=1s$

$\Delta t=4-1=3s$,

$v=\sqrt{2gh}=\sqrt{2\times 9.8\times 4.9}=9.8$ m/s

$\therefore$ depth $=9.8\times 3=29.4$ m

text: One end of a massless spring of spring constant k and natural length $l_{0}$ is fixed while the other end is connected to a small object of mass m lying on a frictionless table. text:
According to kinetic theory of gases,

A. The motion of the gas molecules freezes at 0${}^{\circ }$C.

B. The mean free path of gas molecules decreases if the density of molecules is increased.

C. The mean free path of gas molecules increases if temperature is increased keeping pressure constant.

D. Average kinetic energy per molecule per degree of freedom is $\frac{3}{2}k_{B}T$ (for monoatomic gases).

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to kinetic theory of gases,

A. The motion of the gas molecules freezes at 0 K.

B. The mean free path decreases on increasing the number density of the molecules as $μ=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}πnd^{2}}\Rightarrow μ\propto \frac{1}{n}$.

C. The mean free path increases on increasing the volume. Now if temperature is increased by keeping the pressure constant the volume should increase that is mean free path increases.

$D. K.E._{$avg} per molecule per degree of freedom is $\frac{1}{2}k_{B}T$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

A lead bullet penetrates into a solid object and melts. Assuming that 40% of its kinetic energy is used to heat it, the initial speed of bullet is :

$\Rightarrow \frac{v^{2}}{5}=2.5\times 10^{4}+125\times 200$

$\Rightarrow \frac{v^{2}}{5}=5\times 10^{4}$

$\Rightarrow v=500$ m/s

text:
Two long parallel conductors $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ are separated by a distance 10 cm and carrying currents of 4A and 2A respectively. The conductors are placed along x-axis in X-Y plane. There is a point P located between the conductors (as shown in figure).

A charged particle of 3$π$ coulomb is passing through the point P with velocity $\vec{v}=(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j})$ m/s; where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ represents unit vector along x & y axis respectively.

The force acting on the charged particle is $4π\times 10^{-5}(-x\hat{i}+2\hat{j})$ N. The value of x is :

 
[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Field at P is $=\left (\frac{μ_{0}\times i_{1}}{2πr_{1}}-\frac{μ_{0}i_{2}}{2πr_{2}}\right )\left (-\widehat{k}\right )$

$=-\left (\frac{μ_{0}4}{2π\times 0.04}-\frac{μ_{0}\times 2}{2π\times 0.06}\right )\widehat{k}=-\frac{μ_{0}\times 200}{6π}\widehat{k}$

So, force $\vec{F}=q\vec{v}\times \vec{B}$

$=3π\left (2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}\right )\times \left (-\left (\frac{μ_{0}\times 200}{6π}\widehat{k}\right )\right )$

$=3π\left (\frac{200μ_{0}}{3π}\hat{j}-\frac{100μ_{0}}{π}\hat{i}\right )$

$=200μ_{0}\hat{j}-300μ_{0}\hat{i}$

$=4π\times 10^{-5}(2\hat{j}-3\hat{i})$

So, $x=3$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : In hydrogen atom, the frequency of radiation emitted when an electron jumps from lower energy orbit $(E_{1})$ to higher energy orbit $(E_{2})$, is given as $hf = E_{1}$ $-$ $E_{2}$

Statement II : The jumping of electron from higher energy orbit $(E_{2})$ to lower energy orbit $(E_{1})$ is associated with frequency of radiation given as $f = (E_{2}$ $-$ $E_{1})/h$

This condition is Bohr's frequency condition.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Radiation is not emitted but absorbed when an electron jumps from low energy to high energy.

Also, $E_{2}$ $-$ $E_{1}$ is the energy of photon

$\Rightarrow$ $E_{2}$ $-$ $E_{1} = hf$

$\Rightarrow f=\frac{E_{2}-E_{1}}{h}$

text:
A mass of 10  kg is suspended vertically by a rope of length 5 m from the roof. A force of 30 N is applied at the middle point of rope in horizontal direction. The angle made by upper half of the rope with vertical is $θ$ $= \tan ^{-1} (x$ $\times$ $10^{-1})$. The value of x is $____________$.

(Given, $g = 10 m/s^{2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


The vertical component of the tension, $T\cos θ$, balances the weight of the mass:

$T\cos θ=mg$

Since $mg=10\text{kg}\times 10\text{m/s}^{2}=100\text{N}$:

$T\cos θ=100\text{N}$ ...... (i)

The horizontal component of the tension is given by:

$T\sin θ=30\text{N}$ ........ (ii)

Dividing equation (ii) by equation (i):

$\frac{T\sin θ}{T\cos θ}=\frac{30}{100}$

Therefore:

$\tan θ=\frac{3}{10}$

Hence, the value of x is:

$\therefore x=3$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

text:
A rolling wheel of 12 kg is on an inclined plane at position P and connected to a mass of 3 kg through a string of fixed length and pulley as shown in figure. Consider PR as friction free surface. The velocity of centre of mass of the wheel when it reaches at the bottom Q of the inclined plane PQ will be $\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{xgh}$ m/s. The value of x is $___________$.

 
[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Taking the wheel as a ring ($I=MR^{2}$) rolling without slipping on PQ, the string attached at its axle moves the $3\text{kg}$ block up the frictionless incline PR at the same speed $v$ and through the same distance, so the block rises by $h$ while the wheel descends by $h$.

Energy conservation from rest:

$12gh-3gh=\dfrac{1}{2}(12)v^{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}\left (12R^{2}\right )\dfrac{v^{2}}{R^{2}}+\dfrac{1}{2}(3)v^{2}$

$9gh=13.5v^{2}\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{3}}=\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{8}{3}gh}$

So $x=\dfrac{8}{3}\approx 2.67$, which to the nearest integer is 3.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

text:
In the given circuit 'a' is an arbitrary constant. The value of m for which the equivalent circuit resistance is minimum, will be $\sqrt{\frac{x}{2}}$. The value of x is $__________$.

$=a\left [\frac{m}{3}+\frac{1}{2m}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}\right ]$

$=a\left [\left (\sqrt{\frac{m}{3}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2m}}\right )^{2}+\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\right ]$

This will be minimum when

$\sqrt{\frac{m}{3}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2m}}$

or $m=\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}$

so $x=3$
